name: IronGlass Soviet Rehoused MKII
productionYears: MKII rehousing generation active in the 2020s; based on much older Soviet still-photography donor optics.
publicSummary: IronGlass Soviet Rehoused MKII lenses turn Soviet still-photography optics like Mir, Helios, Jupiter and Tair into modern cine-style lenses with PL-mount mechanics, unified fronts, T-stop markings and a strong painterly character.
coverage: Stills-derived optics; commonly treated as full-frame capable, but exact usable image circle and corner behavior vary by donor lens, copy, focus distance and rehousing.
mounts: LPL/EF options depending on custom order or adapter system
closeFocus: Improved close focus compared with original stills mechanics; exact values vary by focal length, donor and rehousing batch. Verify copy-specific values before publication.

focalLengthSpecs.notes: Full-frame fisheye with 180-degree field of view; highly distorted artistic perspective.
Widest rectilinear Soviet lens in the lineup; Flektogon-based rendering with deep perspective and soft edge falloff.
Faster 20mm option with large image circle and stronger modern production usefulness.
Neutral wide option with subtle contrast, minimal distortion and warm side-light flare.
Close-focus 35mm with detailed rendering, smooth bokeh and useful low-light speed.
Flektogon-derived 37mm with improved MKII close focus and strong flare/contrast character.
Sharper, more controlled Biotar-family Helios option with stronger contrast than Helios 44-2.
Signature focal length with plasticity, iconic swirl and vintage mechanical flaws removed by the MKII body.
Fast cult portrait lens with iconic swirling bokeh, smooth focus falloff and strong portrait character.
Sonnar-derived 85mm with smooth, round bokeh and expressive portrait softness.
Long telephoto option with vintage compression, warm contrast and expressive falloff.

coating: Vintage Soviet coatings; internal coating options may vary by rehousing/custom order.
designFamily: Rehoused Soviet still-photography optics: Mir, Helios, Jupiter, Tair and related designs.
donorLens: MIR-20M, MIR-10A, MIR-1B, Helios 77M-4, Helios 44-2, Jupiter-9, Tair-11A and related Soviet optics depending on set.
rehousingInfo: MKII uses redesigned cine mechanics with internal/hybrid focus, universal gear positions, shimmable PL mount, 15-blade iris, T-stop markings and a 95mm front in common 7-lens sets.
lookSummary: Painterly, organic and imperfect: sharp center with gentle edge falloff, swirly bokeh, lower contrast, warm/rich tones and very expressive flares.
characteristics: Modern cine mechanics over vintage donor glass
strengths: Huge character per euro compared with major-brand vintage sets
Modern rehousing makes Soviet optics practical on set
Strong association with recent high-end blockbuster texture
Great for music videos, stylized drama and dirty/organic digital images
weaknesses: Not optically uniform like modern matched primes
Focal lengths and donors vary by set
Exact specs can differ by batch/custom options
Project Hail Mary credit currently needs verification
Can flare or fall apart too much for clean commercial work
